head_commit.message:
fix(build): provision googletest for linux-x64-native and linux-x64-reference (M2-N1/ENG-35138)

root_cause: foundation-dll smoke on Linux compiles tests/unit/runtime-native
gtest tests (gc_bit_utils, etc.), but neither linux-x64-native nor
linux-x64-reference branches in CMakeLists.txt provisioned googletest.  The
build died with 'fatal error: gtest/gtest.h: No such file or directory' at the
first gtest include in gc_bit_utils_test.cpp.

The windows-x64-reference branch had googletest (added when the CI round-7
gtest_main.lib fix was applied), and linux-arm64-native also had it (added for
the ARM64 JIT test harness), but the two x64 Linux branches were overlooked.

fix_strategy: add FetchContent googletest block (same URL_HASH as the Windows
branch, with gtest_force_shared_crt OFF for GCC) to both linux-x64-reference
and linux-x64-native branches, before fmt or any subdirectory that transitively
depends on gtest.

regression_check: same pattern as windows-x64-reference (line 77) and
linux-arm64-native (line 564) — confirmed working on those branches.

fix(ci): grant docs-deploy its Pages permissions at the caller (M2-N1/ENG-35138)

root_cause: 'startup_failure' on every pipeline dispatch after 517abca01.  A
reusable workflow invoked with 'uses:' cannot request more permissions than the
calling job grants; pipeline.yml called docs-deploy.yml without a permissions
block, so the run got the default read-only GITHUB_TOKEN and the workflow
failed validation before any job started.  Declaring permissions inside
docs-deploy.yml alone is not enough — the grant must come from the caller.
This is the same pattern already used for gc-stress / gc-perf / jit-baseline
(contents: write) and codeql (security-events: write).

fix_strategy: add permissions: {pages: write, id-token: write} to the
docs-deploy dispatcher job in pipeline.yml.

regression_check: YAML parses; dispatch now starts instead of startup_failure.

fix(ci): restore docs Doxyfile + Pages id-token permission (M2-N1/ENG-35138)

root_cause (two independent defects behind the docs-build/docs-deploy failures):
1. docs/native-api/Doxyfile did not exist.  It was added by 7ca967c45 then
   lost in the ci-r7-clean tree overwrite.  'doxygen <missing-file>' prints
   help text and exits 1, so docs-build could never succeed.
2. docs-deploy uses actions/deploy-pages@v4 which authenticates via OIDC;
   without id-token: write it fails with 'Unable to get
   ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL env variable'.
3. Repo-level Pages was never enabled (API 404 'Not Found').

fix_strategy:
1. Restore Doxyfile + README from 7ca967c45; verified both INPUT paths
   (contracts/native/v0, src/native/common/chaos) exist.
2. Add pages: write + id-token: write to the docs-deploy job.
3. Enabled Pages on the repo with build_type=workflow (out-of-band API call).

regression_check: this is the first run where docs-build can reach the doxygen
invocation at all; docs-deploy next run should proceed past OIDC.

fix(publish): sanitize method name in DeriveEntryCall for async/top-level entry

Roslyn generates <Main>$ / <Main> for async Task Main entry points
(and <Main>$ for top-level statements).  The DeriveEntryCall method used
the bare SubjectId method name (e.g. "<Main>") to construct the proxy
call, producing:
  AsyncDemo2_Program::<Main>(chaos_args)  // C2589: '<' illegal

The codegen-emitted proxy struct uses the sanitized name _Main_ instead
(Sanitize replaces punctuation with underscores).  Sanitize the method
name before constructing the proxy call expression, matching what the
generated chaos_generated_module.h actually exports.

regression_check: samples/HelloWorld publish -> entry.exe -> 'Hello from
chaos-il2cpp!' exit 0.  Named-class sync Main is unaffected (method name
contains no punctuation, Sanitize is idempotent).
